_about: The curated prayers for each stretch of Recovery Road (Paul's ruling, 2026-08-26). Twenty-five per station, hand-picked from that station's pool against its own material -- recovery lens, life lens, hope, one next action, your-response questions, hard questions, and the pastoral guardrail. Hope first. Ids only: the prayer text still lives once, in the catalog. The stations are mutually exclusive -- a prayer picked here is off the table for every station curated after it -- and they are curated smallest-pool first so the constrained stations pick before the wide ones strip the shelf.
_order: Most relevant first. The screen shows 8, then 8 more, then the final 9.

prayers.title: Exercise for Abstinence
prayers.why: Paul's pin. The Nazirite's own abstinence pledge, at the Nazirite's station.

prayers.title: In a Slippery Place
prayers.why: Paul's pin. 'I stand in a slippery place, and am surrounded on every side with snares.'

prayers.title: Almighty God, Who Seest That We Have No Power of Ourselves
prayers.why: Step One in liturgical form -- 'no power of ourselves to help ourselves' -- and it is the real BCP collect, not a corpus rewrite.

prayers.title: Third Step Prayer - AA Big Book 1939
prayers.why: The Third Step Prayer. 'Relieve me of the bondage of self' is the answer to a man whose own strength put him at the mill.

prayers.title: The Serenity Prayer (Long Form)
prayers.why: One Serenity Prayer out of the five in this pool. The long form carries the famous three lines AND one-day-at-a-time, which is this station's whole discipline.

prayers.title: Way of the Cross - Station 7: Jesus Falls Second Time
prayers.why: The only prayer in the catalog that names relapse outright: 'by Thy second fall, preserve me from relapsing into sin.' Short enough to say at the edge.

prayers.title: Lead me not into these temptations
prayers.why: 'For Thou art the powerful, and the battle is Thine. Fight, O Lord.' Powerlessness answered by somebody else's strength.

prayers.title: O Lord, Without Thee I Can Do Nothing
prayers.why: 'Resist mightily the very first beginnings of evil, before it takes hold of me' -- the small permissions in the station's own brief, named exactly.

prayers.title: A Prayer for a Penitent
prayers.why: 'Castest not out whatever comes to thee, but graciously receivest, cherishest, and refreshest it.' Hope for a man who expects to be turned away.

prayers.title: We Confess Unto Thee, O God, How Weak We Are in Ourselves
prayers.why: 'How weak we are in ourselves, how powerless to do the work of life' -- and then strength asked for. Step One moving into Step Two.

prayers.title: Evening Purpose of Amendment
prayers.why: 'Thou who givest me the will, give me also the power to perform.' The will is there; the power is not. That is the mill.

prayers.title: O God, the Strength of the Weak, the Friend of Sinners
prayers.why: 'The Strength of the weak, the Friend of sinners... give the consolation of Thy presence to those who are disappointed, embittered, lonely, or in despair.'

prayers.title: Lord, My God, Light of the Blind and Strength of the Weak
prayers.why: Augustine: 'Light of the blind and Strength of the weak.' Samson was blinded at that mill -- and it closes 'Thou hast not forsaken Thy creatures as we have forsaken Thee.'

prayers.title: O Lord, Shield of Our Help, Who Wilt Not Suffer Us to Be Tempted Above That We Are Able
prayers.why: Rossetti, and short: 'who wilt not suffer us to be tempted above that we are able.' A promise, not a demand.

prayers.title: For Steadfastness — Thomas Aquinas
prayers.why: Aquinas: 'an unconquered heart, which no tribulation can wear out' -- for a man whose strength has become strain.

prayers.title: A Petition Against Human Frailty
prayers.why: 'By reason of the frailty of our nature we cannot always stand upright' -- said plainly, at the station where willpower has already failed. (Reason rewritten 2026-08-27: it used to rest on 'making us willing to be kept by Thee', which was a grafted line and has been removed in favour of the collect's real ending.)

prayers.title: Merciful Lord, Enlighten Thou Me With a Clear Shining Inward Light
prayers.why: a Kempis: 'Fight Thou for me, and vanquish the evil beasts, that so peace may be obtained by Thy power.'

prayers.title: Heavenly Father, Subdue in Me Whatever Is Contrary to Thy Holy Will
prayers.why: 'Grant that I may never run into those temptations which in my prayers I desire to avoid.' The honest one -- do not let me walk into it.

prayers.title: Morning Avoidance of Sin (Name Your Occasions)
prayers.why: The name-your-own-occasions exercise. Answers the station's question about which boundary was traded away, in the form of a prayer.

prayers.title: A Prayer against Gluttony and Drunkenness
prayers.why: Names drink without shaming: 'suffer me not by my folly to change thy bounty into sin, thy grace into wantonness.'

prayers.title: For Temperance
prayers.why: The most direct text in the pool -- 'captives who are in bondage to drunkenness' -- and it prays for them as fellows, which is the program's own posture.

prayers.title: Tishbukhta for Monday (Mar Abraham)
prayers.why: 'Thou art the refuge and hope of the weak... he at all times setteth snares for our souls.' The Eastern voice, and the same snares as the pinned prayer.

prayers.title: O God, Who Hast Enkindled in the Holy Bosoms of All Thy Saints So Great an Ardor of Faith
prayers.why: 'That the hateful sweetness of sin may wax faint in us, and we may glow with the infused warmth of love for Thee.' The best line on craving in the pool.

prayers.title: We Give Thee Thanks, Yea, More Than Thanks
prayers.why: 'Thou hast shielded, rescued, helped, and guided us all the days of our lives, and brought us unto this hour.' Gratitude for having got this far.

prayers.title: Jesus, Walk Me All the Way Home
prayers.why: Paul's own, and the right closer: 'don't leave me in the grip of my weakness... let me follow You faithfully to the end.'

prayers.title: Prayer for Restitution and Amendment
prayers.why: Paul's pin. Restitution and amendment, named outright.

prayers.title: For Those I Have Harmed or Led Astray
prayers.why: Paul's pin. Prays for the people he harmed rather than for his own relief.

prayers.title: A Prayer for Honest Restitution
prayers.why: Zacchaeus, who promised fourfold restoration. The only prayer in the pool about paying it back rather than feeling bad about it.

prayers.title: A Prayer to Be Made Whole
prayers.why: 'Forgive what I have been, sanctify what I am, and order what I shall be.' The rebuild in one sentence.

prayers.title: If They Say No
prayers.why: 'Turn it into love I can act on.' When grief has to become a plan, and the other person may still say no.

prayers.title: Hebraic Prayer for Willingness to Seek Atonement from Man
prayers.why: 'Before I ask atonement from Thee, I must ask it of those I have wronged.' Step 9's whole principle, in a Jewish voice.

prayers.title: In the Sight of This Man
prayers.why: Nehemiah's own prayer before he faced the king, in Paul's words: 'Let me find mercy... in the eyes of the one I need to face. And give me what it takes today to make it right.' The amends conversation, from this station's own book. Paul's pick, 2026-09-28, in place of an 'AA Step 8 & 9' prayer that is not in the 1939 book.

prayers.title: Morning Prayer for Willingness to Amend
prayers.why: 'As I go forth this day, let me remember my duty to amend.' Daily work, which is what a wall is.

prayers.title: Putting It Off
prayers.why: Leave the gift at the altar and go first: the amend before the devotion, and no more putting it off.

prayers.title: For Reparation Without Injury
prayers.why: For reparation WITHOUT injury. The station's guardrail said as a prayer: repair is not permission to hurt someone again.

prayers.title: To Do No Hurt to My Neighbor
prayers.why: 'To do no hurt to my neighbour.' The other half of the same guardrail.

prayers.title: I Will Be No Longer Mine Own
prayers.why: Wesley's covenant: 'Put me to doing, put me to suffering.' A rebuilder's surrender is to the work, not away from it.

prayers.title: Prayer for Humility to Make Amends
prayers.why: 'Take away my pride which hinders me from confessing my wrong to my brother.' Names the actual obstacle.

prayers.title: Swallowing My Pride
prayers.why: Humility to OWN the fault, backbone to FIX it. Two different graces, and it asks for both.

prayers.title: Methodist Prayer for Readiness to Confess
prayers.why: 'Bring to remembrance my offences against my neighbour. Help me to number them.' This is the list being made.

prayers.title: To Make Others the Happier
prayers.why: 'Grant that each one who has to do with me today may be the happier for it.' Forward repair -- the wall going up, not the rubble.

prayers.title: Final Prayer of Willingness to Complete Amends
prayers.why: 'Now make me willing to repair them wholly.' Willing to see was step eight; willing to finish is this.

prayers.title: For Keeping Word to Those Wronged
prayers.why: To desire, search out, and fulfil -- keeping his word to the people he wronged.

prayers.title: For Direct Amends
prayers.why: For direct amends, plainly.

prayers.title: I Offer Up Unto Thee My Prayers and Intercessions
prayers.why: Intercession for those he has hurt or grieved. Praying for them costs nothing and asks nothing of them.

prayers.title: Gallican Sacramentary - Prayer for Amendment of Life
prayers.why: 'What we have promised in words, we may fulfil in deeds.' The gap this station lives in.

prayers.title: Quaker Prayer for Willingness to Repair
prayers.why: 'Show me wherein I have wronged my fellow.' Quaker, plain, and short enough to mean.

prayers.title: Check My Reasons
prayers.why: 'Let my amends be for the people I hurt, not for me.' The motive check before the wall goes up.

prayers.title: For Rectitude in Dealing
prayers.why: 'To be that which Thou wouldst have us to be, and to do that which Thou wouldst have us do' -- this day, again.

prayers.title: Prayer for Amendment of Life
prayers.why: 'I have wasted enough time.' The urgency without the panic.

prayers.title: Oh, God! Behold My Grief and Care. Fain Would I Serve Thee With a Glad and Cheerful Countenance
prayers.why: 'Fain would I serve Thee with a glad and cheerful countenance, but I cannot.' This station's first hard question is about pretending to be spiritually fine. Here is the prayer that refuses to.

prayers.title: On the Loss of a Beloved One Morning - Annie Josephine Levi 1900
prayers.why: 'Thou hast taken from me one whom I loved. My heart is sore and my eyes are dim with tears.' Names the loss and stops. No explanation offered, which is the whole guardrail.

prayers.title: Let my darkness be enlightened
prayers.why: Nine words: 'O Lord, my God, let my darkness be enlightened.' Some days that is the most a man can say, and it should be on the first screen.

prayers.title: Psalm 129 - De Profundis - Out of the Depths
prayers.why: De Profundis. Out of the depths, which is where he is standing.

prayers.title: Lord! When I Am in Sorrow I Think on Thee
prayers.why: 'Listen to the cry of my heart, and my sorrowful complaint.' Arguing WITH God -- still in the relationship -- which the hard questions distinguish from walking away.

prayers.title: May He Support Us All the Day Long
prayers.why: 'Till the shades lengthen, and the evening comes... then in His mercy may He give us safe lodging, and a holy rest, and peace at the last.' If it belongs anywhere, it belongs here.

prayers.title: For Hope in Affliction
prayers.why: 'Thou dost not willingly afflict or grieve the children of men.' Lamentations 3:33 -- the one answer this station is allowed to give, because it refuses to blame him.

prayers.title: Thou Hast Visited Us Through the Angel of Death
prayers.why: 'Thou hast visited us through the angel of death, taking from us the familiar face of one who belonged in...' Bereavement said plainly.

prayers.title: O Lord, My God! The Amazing Horrors of Darkness Were Gathered Round Me
prayers.why: 'The amazing horrors of darkness were gathered round me, and covered me all over.' Someone else has been this far down and wrote it out.

prayers.title: Thou Understandest All Thy Children
prayers.why: 'Thou understandest all thy children... we bring our perplexities.' Presence rather than an answer.

prayers.title: Almighty God, Have Compassion, We Pray Thee, Upon All Those Whose Hearts Are Touched With Sorrow
prayers.why: For all those whose hearts are touched with sorrow -- prayed for him when he cannot pray for himself.

prayers.title: We Beseech Thee, O Lord, Give Strength to the Weary
prayers.why: Twenty-five words: strength to the weary, aid to the sufferers, comfort to the sad.

prayers.title: Comfort, We Beseech Thee, Most Gracious God, Thy Servants Who Are Cast Down and Faint of Heart
prayers.why: For servants cast down and faint of heart. He may not think of himself as a servant today; the prayer does.

prayers.title: For Those in Mental Darkness
prayers.why: For those living in mental darkness. Grief and depression are not the same thing and this station meets both.

prayers.title: O God, Who Remainest the Same Though All Else Fades
prayers.why: 'Who remainest the same though all else fades, who changest not with our changing moods.' For a man whose whole world just changed.

prayers.title: In Time of Trouble
prayers.why: 'My heart is heavy and my spirit is weighed down.' Annie Josephine Levi, 1900, and she does not try to fix it either.

prayers.title: Let Thy Merciful Kindness Be for My Comfort
prayers.why: Eighteen words. 'Let Thy merciful kindness be for my comfort.'

prayers.title: Psalm 101 - Domine exaudi - Hear my prayer
prayers.why: Psalm 102: 'Turn not away Thy face from me.' The fear underneath the grief.

prayers.title: Almighty and Everlasting God, the Comfort of the Sad, the Strength of Sufferers
prayers.why: 'The Comfort of the sad, the Strength of sufferers.' Short, and it asks nothing of him.

prayers.title: Eternal and Unchangeable God, in Whom Alone We Find Rest for Our Weariness
prayers.why: 'In whom alone we find rest for our weariness and comfort for our sorrow.'

prayers.title: O God, We Pray Thee to Have in Thy Holy Keeping Those Precious Souls
prayers.why: For the precious souls nearest and dearest to us who have gone -- his people, held somewhere safe.

prayers.title: Give Rest, O Christ, to the Soul of Thy Servants With Thy Saints
prayers.why: 'Where there is no sickness, nor sorrow.' Twenty-five words, and the only promise it makes is about them, not about him.

prayers.title: We Remember All Those Once Known to Us on the Earth
prayers.why: 'We remember all those once known to us on the earth.' Remembrance without a lesson attached.

prayers.title: Almighty Father, Who Neither Slumberest Nor Sleepest
prayers.why: For the ones sitting up through the night with someone: 'watch over us this night ... and over all who are near and dear to us', then rest on the everlasting arms. Took the place of 'For the Anxious and Sorrowful Watchers', pulled 2026-10-15 (an altered copy of a 1928 collect).

prayers.title: In Thee, O Lord God, I Place My Whole Hope and Refuge
prayers.why: 'On Thee I rest all my tribulation and anguish.' Somewhere to put it down.

prayers.title: Prayer for Willing to be Willing
prayers.why: 'I am not willing, but I am willing to be made willing.' That is a man arguing at a burning bush and not walking off. Nothing else in the pool is this station.

prayers.title: For Courage to Serve
prayers.why: 'Who givest strength to the weary and increasest power to them that have no might.' Isaiah 40, for the man who says he is too old, too late, too damaged.

prayers.title: For Belief That Restoration is Possible
prayers.why: 'With Thee nothing is impossible.' The direct answer to a resume that feels disqualifying.

prayers.title: Prayer for Strength in Willingness
prayers.why: 'I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.' This station's hard question is whom he will let hold up his arms -- which is Exodus 17, two men holding up Moses'.

prayers.title: Prayer for Divine Acceptance
prayers.why: 'I do not ask that Thou shouldst make me acceptable, but that Thou shouldst make me willing.' Refuses to wait until he feels qualified.

prayers.title: Against Anger
prayers.why: Against anger. The station names anger outright -- where it has become justification for control rather than advocacy.

prayers.title: Prayer to Have Defects Removed
prayers.why: 'I have tried to change myself and failed.' The objection said honestly instead of argued.

prayers.title: Bestow Upon Me, O God, That Courage
prayers.why: 'That courage which Thou alone givest, that I may meet serenely whatever comes.'

prayers.title: Almighty God, Give to Thy Servants Meek and Gentle Spirits
prayers.why: 'Swift to hear, slow to speak.' Moses' own objection at the bush was that he could not speak. This turns that into something other than a disqualification.

prayers.title: Father of Mercies and God of All Comfort, Help to Meet the Trials of Advancing Years
prayers.why: 'Our only help in time of need, I come to Thee for help to meet the trial.' Help asked for plainly, which is this station's one next action.

prayers.title: Prayer Before New Life
prayers.why: 'Went not up to joy but first he suffered pain, and entered not into glory before he was crucified.' For the years he is calling wasted that may have been the training.

prayers.title: Prayer to be Made Willing
prayers.why: 'Make our wills ready and our hearts obedient.' Short, and it asks for the readiness rather than claiming it.

prayers.title: A Prayer for Self-Knowledge
prayers.why: 'Show me my true self. Let me not deceive myself concerning my own defects.' Honest inventory without shame doing the talking.

prayers.title: Armenian Prayer for Divine Wisdom — Nerses Shnorhali
prayers.why: Nerses Shnorhali: wisdom to know Thy will, strength to do it, courage to trust. Twenty-eight words, and an Armenian voice on a shelf that leans Latin.

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Augustine - Remove Self
prayers.why: 'Purged of all self-seeking and self-will. Grant me humility to confess my faults.' Augustine, and the humility asked for is for confessing, not for hiding.

prayers.title: Prayer for Willing Mind
prayers.why: 'A willing mind, to do Thy work cheerfully, to bear my cross patiently.' The work in front of him, not the work he wishes he had.

prayers.title: Prayer for Willing Service of Others
prayers.why: 'Willing to serve my neighbour, to bear his burden.' A limitation can require support without cancelling purpose -- and support runs both directions.

prayers.title: A Prayer for Devotion to Service
prayers.why: 'A wise, a sober, a patient, an understanding, a devout, a religious, a courageous heart.' The whole list of what he thinks he lacks.

prayers.title: Prayer for Willing Spirit Psalm
prayers.why: 'Teach me to do thy will... lead me into the land of uprightness.' Psalm 143, asking for the road rather than the destination.

prayers.title: Prayer for Willing Surrender Daily
prayers.why: 'This day, O Lord, I give myself anew to Thee.' Anew -- which matters to a man with a relapse history.

prayers.title: Prayer for Removal of Self-Will
prayers.why: 'From the fear that clings to my defects.' Names the fear of letting the defect go, which is a different thing from the defect.

prayers.title: Prayer for Humility and Patience
prayers.why: 'That I may bear with the infirmities of others as Thou bearest with mine.' The accommodation he wants, offered outward.

prayers.title: Against Sloth
prayers.why: Against sloth, from a man who 'shun no labour'. For the objection that has stopped being an objection and become a place to sit.

prayers.title: Prayer for Yielding
prayers.why: 'Be pliant in His hands as clay.' Yielding without being crushed.

prayers.title: Prayer of Complete Surrender
prayers.why: 'My body, my soul, my mind, my will, my past, my present, my future.' My past is the word this station turns on.

prayers.title: Aspiration before Any Work
prayers.why: Paul's pin. Aspiration before any work -- said before the doing, which is where formation belongs.

prayers.title: Some Definite Service
prayers.why: 'I have my mission... I am a link in a chain, a bond of connexion between persons.' A past that becomes a purpose without pretending it was not a past. This station in one prayer.

prayers.title: A Morning Prayer for Pure Intention
prayers.why: For pure intention. The hard question here is whether the testimony serves the listener or secures attention -- this is the prayer that asks.

prayers.title: For Usefulness and Humility
prayers.why: For usefulness AND humility, in the same breath. The guardrail warns against premature leadership sounding spiritually superior; this refuses to separate the two.

prayers.title: To Be Servants of All
prayers.why: 'To be servants of all.' The man led by the hand into Damascus had been the one giving orders.

prayers.title: Lord, Take My Lips and Speak Through Them; Take My Mind, and Think Through It
prayers.why: 'Take my lips and speak through them; take my mind, and think through them.' Twenty-four words, and every one of them redirects the intensity instead of suppressing it.

prayers.title: Prayer to Carry the Message
prayers.why: To carry the message -- the Twelfth Step's own verb, and the thing this station is learning to do safely.

prayers.title: For Grace to Carry Principles into Action
prayers.why: 'Grace to carry principles into action.' Not to talk about them.

prayers.title: For Humble Service
prayers.why: For humble service. Ananias is the model here: he went to the man who had been arresting his friends.

prayers.title: To Live Not for Self
prayers.why: 'To live not for self.' The correction a redirected zealot needs most and hears least.

prayers.title: To Practice Principles in Daily Life
prayers.why: To practice principles in daily life -- the unglamorous half, after the testimony is told.

prayers.title: For Help to Help Others
prayers.why: For help to help others. Asks for the help first, which is the order this station insists on.

prayers.title: Almighty God, Who Didst Give Such Grace to the First Followers of Thy Son
prayers.why: For the grace given to the first followers -- Paul was the last of them and the least likely.

prayers.title: Lord, Do Thou Turn Me All Into Love
prayers.why: 'Turn me all into love.' Intensity given a direction rather than a brake.

prayers.title: Master of the Hearts of Men
prayers.why: Master of the hearts of men. For a man who once thought he could change hearts by force.

prayers.title: To Conquer Faults and Serve Better
prayers.why: To conquer faults AND serve better. This station's people try to skip the first half.

prayers.title: For Those Who Are Lost
prayers.why: For those who are lost -- the people he used to be certain about.

prayers.title: Mould Us, Great God, Into Forms of Beauty and Usefulness
prayers.why: 'Mould us into forms of beauty and usefulness.' Formation, which is the word the guardrail uses.

prayers.title: For Opportunity to Serve
prayers.why: For opportunity to serve, rather than for a platform.

prayers.title: For Daily Usefulness
prayers.why: 'To pass this day usefully and without sin.' Today, not the testimony tour.

prayers.title: Lord of Hosts, Help Us to Do Our Small Part
prayers.why: 'Help us to do our small part.' The correction to a man whose part has always felt enormous.

prayers.title: For the Spirit of Self-Sacrifice
prayers.why: For the spirit of self-sacrifice -- offered, not performed.

prayers.title: Lord Jesus Christ, the Good Shepherd, Who Didst Lay Down Thy Life for the Sheep
prayers.why: The Good Shepherd who laid down His life for the sheep. The standard against which zeal is measured.

prayers.title: Give Us This Day a Collected Mind and a Tender Conscience
prayers.why: 'A collected mind and a tender conscience.' Both of which this station says need forming.

prayers.title: I Delight to Do Thy Will, O My God
prayers.why: Sixteen words: 'I delight to do Thy will, O my God.' Where the intensity is supposed to end up.

prayers.title: When I See Good in My Neighbour
prayers.why: Paul's pin. The encourager's prayer -- what to do with the good you notice in someone else.

prayers.title: When I See Wrong in My Neighbour
prayers.why: Its pair, and the harder half: what to do when you see WRONG in your neighbour. Barnabas vouched for Paul without pretending Paul had been harmless.

prayers.title: Way of the Cross - Station 5: Simon Helps Jesus Carry Cross
prayers.why: Simon of Cyrene, pulled out of the crowd to carry a stranger's cross. The same story from the other side of the door.

prayers.title: O Lord, Who Lovest the Stranger
prayers.why: 'O Lord, who lovest the stranger.' This station asks whom he overlooks because helping them offers no status.

prayers.title: Thou, Who Satisfiest the Desires of the Hearts That Thou Hast Made
prayers.why: The helper who needs help: 'who refreshest those who are weary', then 'care for every one for whom Thou carest'. William Angus Knight. Took the place of 'For Rest for the Weary Caregiver', pulled 2026-10-15 (no source).

prayers.title: Pour Into Our Hearts the Spirit of Unselfishness
prayers.why: 'Pour into our hearts the spirit of unselfishness.' Against the hard question -- do I help because he needs it, or because I need to be central.

prayers.title: That We May Bear One Another's Burdens
prayers.why: To bear one another's burdens. Bearing, not carrying off.

prayers.title: Exercise for Love of Our Neighbour
prayers.why: Love of neighbour worked as an exercise rather than felt as a mood.

prayers.title: To Be a Comfort and Joy
prayers.why: To be a comfort and a joy. Two things a man can be without fixing anybody.

prayers.title: To Make Life Happier for Others
prayers.why: To make life happier for others -- the bounded act this station asks for.

prayers.title: The Dignity of Common Life
prayers.why: The people already doing the work without a title: 'dignify by Thy presence and aid the trivial round and common tasks'. Bishop Brent, 1907. Took the place of 'For Volunteers and Community Caregivers', pulled 2026-10-15 (a modern, copyrighted prayer).

prayers.title: Strengthen Us, We Beseech Thee, O Heavenly Father, That Rejoicing in the Goodness of Other People
prayers.why: Close in, where it is hardest: 'rejoicing in the goodness of other people we may be kept from envy and jealousy'. Barnabas's whole gift. Took the place of 'For Charity Toward Neighbors and Friends', pulled 2026-10-15 (no source).

prayers.title: O Lord, Move Us by Thine Example to Show Kindness and Do Good
prayers.why: 'Move us by Thine example to show kindness.' The example, not the instinct to take over.

prayers.title: For Love in Service
prayers.why: For love in service, which is the difference between helping and managing.

prayers.title: Prayer for Those Who Serve Others
prayers.why: For those who serve others -- prayed for the helper, which this station insists on.

prayers.title: Lord, Who Hast Taught Us That All Our Doings Without Charity Are Nothing Worth
prayers.why: 'All our doings without charity are nothing worth.' The measure that outranks the effort.

prayers.title: Almighty God, Who Thyself Art Love; Fill Us With the Spirit of Thy Holy Love
prayers.why: 'Fill us with the spirit of Thy love.' Short and it asks to be filled rather than to be needed.

prayers.title: Prayer to Be Helpful to Our Neighbors
prayers.why: To be helpful to our neighbours. Plainly, without a programme.

prayers.title: O God, Fulfil Every Need of Theirs
prayers.why: Thirty-five words: 'Fulfil every need of theirs.' Theirs, as they name it -- not as he would name it for them.

prayers.title: Lord, Relieve the Wants of Others
prayers.why: Twelve words. 'Lord, relieve the wants of others.' Sometimes that is the whole prayer he has.

prayers.title: Soften Our Hearts, O Lord, That We May Be Moved No Less at the Necessities and Griefs of Our Neighbors
prayers.why: 'Soften our hearts, that we may be moved.' Before the doing, the noticing.

prayers.title: That We May Be Channels of Thy Grace
prayers.why: To be channels of grace -- a channel does not own what passes through it.

prayers.title: Glory when I can give
prayers.why: Seventeen words from Isaac of Nineveh on giving. Short enough to say in a doorway.

prayers.title: O God, the Shepherd of All Thy People
prayers.why: 'O God, the Shepherd of all Thy people.' A reminder about whose sheep they actually are.

prayers.title: For the Grace of Giving
prayers.why: For the grace of giving. Grace, because on the days it is not there he still has to.

prayers.title: Exercise for Peace and Tranquillity of Soul
prayers.why: Paul's pin. Peace and tranquillity of soul, at the station where the soul has stopped cooperating.

prayers.title: O Lord God Almighty, Who Givest Power to the Faint
prayers.why: 'Who givest power to the faint.' Isaiah 40, and the verse this whole station stands on -- exhaustion is not a verdict.

prayers.title: God of Our Life, There Are Days When the Burdens We Carry Chafe Our Shoulders
prayers.why: 'There are days when the burdens we carry...' Names the day rather than diagnosing the man.

prayers.title: O Lord, Who Art as the Shadow of a Great Rock in a Weary Land
prayers.why: 'As the shadow of a great rock in a weary land.' Shade, which is what Elijah got before he got instructions.

prayers.title: For Rest from Weariness
prayers.why: 'Let me not seek out of Thee what I can find only in Thee -- peace and rest.' For the crash after the milestone.

prayers.title: Lord, We Thank Thee for Thine Inward Voice
prayers.why: 'We thank Thee for Thine inward voice.' The hard question here is what quiet answer he is overlooking while demanding a dramatic sign. This is the still small voice as a prayer.

prayers.title: Be Not Weary of Me, Good Lord
prayers.why: 'Be not weary of me, good Lord.' The fear underneath -- that his tiredness has used up someone's patience.

prayers.title: May We Be Still, and Know That Thou Art God
prayers.why: 'May we be still, and know that Thou art God.' Not do. Be still.

prayers.title: Lord, Do Not Permit My Trials to Be Above My Strength
prayers.why: 'Do not permit my trials to be above my strength.' Asking for the load to fit the man, not the man to fit the load.

prayers.title: For Grace in Suffering
prayers.why: 'Who knowest our weakness and wilt not lay upon us more than we can bear.' Weakness named as known, not as failure.

prayers.title: Prayer for Stillness
prayers.why: For stillness. Short, and it asks for nothing else.

prayers.title: Lord, in the Hurry of Everyday Life
prayers.why: 'Lord, in the hurry of everyday life.' He held everyone together; this is the prayer for the day after.

prayers.title: For Quiet Confidence
prayers.why: For quiet confidence. Isaiah 30:15 -- in quietness and confidence shall be your strength.

prayers.title: O God, My God, I Am All Weakness, but Thou Art My Strength
prayers.why: 'I am all weakness, but Thou art my strength.' Said plainly, without apology for the first half.

prayers.title: Give Strength, O Lord, to Those Who Seek Thee
prayers.why: Thirty-seven words: give strength to those who seek Thee. Some days that is the whole capacity.

prayers.title: O God of Strength, Passing All Understanding
prayers.why: 'O God of strength, passing all understanding.' Thirty-five words.

prayers.title: Speak, Lord, for Thy Servant Heareth. Grant Us Ears to Hear, Eyes to See
prayers.why: 'Speak, Lord, for Thy servant heareth.' Listening rather than performing.

prayers.title: Prayer for Conscious Contact
prayers.why: For conscious contact -- the Eleventh Step's own words, and this station's primary resonance.

prayers.title: Grant Us Grace to Rest From All Sinful Deeds and Thoughts
prayers.why: Grace to rest. Rest asked for as a grace, which is what it is when a man cannot let himself take it.

prayers.title: Hilton - Prayer of Quiet
prayers.why: Hilton's prayer of quiet. Fourteenth-century English, and it does not ask him to feel anything.

prayers.title: Night collect: Strengthen our weakness
prayers.why: 'Strengthen our weakness in thy compassion.' Compassion is the operative word -- not correction.

prayers.title: O God, My Heavenly Father, Who Hast Brought Me Thus Far in Safety
prayers.why: 'Who hast brought me thus far.' Behind him is evidence, which is what a crash makes him forget.

prayers.title: O Lord Our God, Under the Shadow of Thy Wings
prayers.why: Under the shadow of Thy wings. Shelter, not a summons.

prayers.title: Now the God of All Grace Who Hath Called Us Unto His Eternal Glory by Christ Jesus
prayers.why: 1 Peter 5:10 -- 'after ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen.' The while is allowed to be a while.

prayers.title: Let the Words of My Mouth
prayers.why: Twenty-four words. 'Let the words of my mouth...' For the day when speech itself is the effort.

prayers.title: Exercise of Hope
prayers.why: Paul's pin. Hope worked as an exercise -- wrestling it through the night rather than waiting to feel it.

prayers.title: Suscipe - Take, Lord and Receive
prayers.why: The Suscipe: 'Take, Lord, and receive.' This station's sharpest question is where he is still trying to TAKE what can only be RECEIVED. Here is the sentence that reverses it.

prayers.title: I Will Whatsoever Thou Willest
prayers.why: Twenty-five words: 'I will whatsoever Thou willest.' The bargain, cancelled, without a counter-offer.

prayers.title: Prayer for Letting Go
prayers.why: For letting go -- the hand that has been gripping since the river.

prayers.title: O God, I Know Not What a Day May Bring Forth
prayers.why: 'I know not what a day may bring forth.' For the man who has always managed the outcome and cannot manage this one.

prayers.title: Prayer for Belief in Greater Power
prayers.why: Belief in a greater power. Step Two said plainly, at the station where his own power ran out.

prayers.title: O Lord, Make Me Love Every Token of Thy Will
prayers.why: 'Make me love every token of Thy will.' Including the limp -- the consequence that stays after the encounter.

prayers.title: Unto Thine Hand I Commit My Spirit
prayers.why: Sixteen words: 'Unto Thine hand I commit my spirit.' Nothing held back and nothing negotiated.

prayers.title: The Serenity Prayer, Singular Voice
prayers.why: Niebuhr's own 1932 wording, before it was smoothed. Accepting what cannot be changed is exactly what a bargainer will not do.

prayers.title: Prayer of Trustful Abandonment
prayers.why: Trustful abandonment. Abandonment is the old word for what he is being asked to risk.

prayers.title: For Grace to Trust
prayers.why: For grace to trust -- because trust is not something he can decide his way into.

prayers.title: Prayer for Inner Yielding
prayers.why: For inner yielding. Not the outward compliance he has been performing.

prayers.title: O Lord, Let Me Not Henceforth Desire Health or Life
prayers.why: 'Let me not henceforth desire health or life, except to spend them for Thee.' The end of the IF/THEN.

prayers.title: Prayer of Fenelon - Simple Abandonment
prayers.why: Fenelon on simple abandonment -- simple being the hard part for a man who has out-thought everything so far.

prayers.title: Make Thy Way Plain Before My Face
prayers.why: 'Make Thy way plain before my face.' Asking for the road instead of engineering one.

prayers.title: Final Prayer - Restoration to Sanity
prayers.why: Restoration to sanity. The hustle has its own logic and this names it as the thing to be restored FROM.

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Francis de Sales - Abandonment
prayers.why: Francis de Sales on abandonment, gentle enough to be heard by someone still braced.

prayers.title: Father, We Trust Thee, We Trust Thee
prayers.why: 'Father, we trust Thee, we trust Thee.' Said twice, the way a man says it when he is trying to mean it.

prayers.title: Quiet Trust - Thy Will
prayers.why: Quiet trust. Quiet, because the noise here is his own negotiating.

prayers.title: Prayer of Entrusting
prayers.why: The prayer of entrusting -- handing over rather than deploying.

prayers.title: O God, Do Thou So Enfold Me in Thy Holy Will
prayers.why: Twenty-seven words: 'Enfold me in Thy holy will.' Clinging, which is what grasping becomes when it gives up.

prayers.title: Collect for Grace to Believe
prayers.why: For grace to believe. He is at the river precisely because believing has not worked as a decision.

prayers.title: Prayer of Yielding to Divine Love
prayers.why: Yielding to divine love, not to a superior force. The difference matters at this station.

prayers.title: Help Me to Resolve, in Thy Strength, That I Will Take Willingly
prayers.why: 'Help me to resolve, in Thy strength.' In Thy strength -- his own is what got him here.

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Thomas More - Divine Amendment
prayers.why: Thomas More on divine amendment, written by a man who knew exactly what he could not out-manoeuvre.

prayers.title: O Lord, Our Hiding Place, Grant Us Wisdom
prayers.why: 'O Lord, our hiding place.' Safety first, which is this station's controlling principle and not a metaphor.

prayers.title: O Lord, Our God, Who Alone Makest Us to Dwell in Safety
prayers.why: 'Who alone makest us to dwell in safety.' Safety is the guardrail's first word, before voice, choice or disclosure.

prayers.title: O Lord, the Keeper of Israel, Who Neither Slumberest Nor Sleepest
prayers.why: 'The Keeper of Israel, who neither slumbereth nor sleepeth.' Psalm 121 -- someone awake while he cannot be.

prayers.title: Psalm 53 - Save Me O God
prayers.why: 'Save me, O God, by Thy name... for strangers are risen up against me.' The psalm says he was harmed. It does not ask him to reframe it.

prayers.title: Gracious Lord, Who Apprehendest the Sighing of a Contrite Heart
prayers.why: 'Who apprehendest the sighing of a contrite heart.' Heard without having to say it out loud -- and this station will not force disclosure.

prayers.title: Be Thou, O God, a Refuge From the Storm
prayers.why: A refuge from the storm. Shelter, not an explanation of the weather.

prayers.title: Protect, O Lord, Thy Suppliants
prayers.why: 'Protect, O Lord, Thy suppliants.' Protection asked for plainly.

prayers.title: Be Thou, O Lord, Our Protection
prayers.why: 'Be Thou, O Lord, our protection.' Short enough to say from inside the pit.

prayers.title: Teach Us to Put Away, O Lord, All Bitterness and Misunderstanding
prayers.why: 'Teach us to put away all bitterness and malice.' The one prayer here about bitterness that asks for HIS freedom rather than the offender's absolution.

prayers.title: Refuge From the Storm
prayers.why: Thirty-nine words. A refuge from the storm, again, because some days he will need it twice.

prayers.title: Grant Unto Us, We Beseech Thee, O Almighty God, the Shelter of Thy Protection
prayers.why: 'The shelter of Thy mercy.' Asks for cover, not for courage he does not have yet.

prayers.title: O Shepherd of the Sheep, Who Didst Promise to Carry the Lambs
prayers.why: The Shepherd who promised to carry the lambs. Carried, not marched.

prayers.title: Compline verses: In thy cross I have taken refuge
prayers.why: 'In thy cross I have taken refuge... protect me from the Evil one and his hosts.' Names that something was done TO him.

prayers.title: For the Absent
prayers.why: For the absent. Joseph was sold away from everyone who knew his name.

prayers.title: O Lord God Almighty, Who Art Our True Peace, and Love Eternal
prayers.why: 'Who art our true peace, and love eternal.' Peace named as a person rather than as a state he has to achieve.

prayers.title: Lord, Who Never Failest to Help and Govern Those Whom Thou Dost Bring Up in Thy Stedfast Fear and Love
prayers.why: 'Who never failest to help and govern those whom Thou dost bring up.' For the years in the house of Potiphar and the years in the cell.

prayers.title: Jesus, Our Master, Do Thou Meet Us
prayers.why: 'Jesus, our Master, do Thou meet us.' Meeting him where he is, which is the only offer this station makes.

prayers.title: Be Thou Present With Me, O Lord, in Every Time and Place
prayers.why: 'Be Thou present with me in every time and place.' Presence, which is what he actually needs and rarely gets.

prayers.title: Night Prayer for God’s Presence and Care
prayers.why: Thirty-three words for the night. Nights are the worst of it.

prayers.title: At Night: the Life of Mortal Men
prayers.why: At night, for the life of mortal men. Plain, and it does not ask him to be grateful for anything.

prayers.title: Be Present, O Lord, to Thy Faithful People
prayers.why: 'Be present, O Lord, to Thy faithful people.' Faithful -- which is what quiet endurance is, even when it feels like nothing.

prayers.title: We Beseech Thee, O Lord, Let the Power of the Holy Spirit Be Present With Us
prayers.why: 'Let the power of the Holy Spirit...' Thirty-six words when there is no strength for more.

prayers.title: Evening Meditation - Annie Josephine Levi 1900
prayers.why: Annie Josephine Levi's evening meditation, 1900. A woman's voice on a shelf that badly needs one.

prayers.title: Hear Us, O Lord, We Beseech Thee, and in Our Tribulations Pity Us
prayers.why: 'In our tribulations, pity us.' Twenty-eight words that ask for pity and not for perspective.

prayers.title: O God, the Consolation of All Such as Be Sorrowful
prayers.why: 'The consolation of all such as be sorrowful.' Consolation offered without a lesson attached to it.

prayers.title: A Prayer Preparatory to Confession
prayers.why: Paul's pin. Its text prays to the One 'who sparedst Peter when he denied thee' -- this station's own name, inside the prayer.

prayers.title: By That Forgiving Tenderness, O Lord, Wherewith Thou Didst Ever Wait for Me
prayers.why: 'By that forgiving tenderness wherewith Thou didst ever wait for me; whenever I wandered, Thou watchedst over me.' Waited for. Not waited out.

prayers.title: I Have Gone Astray Like a Lost Sheep
prayers.why: Psalm 119:176 in eighteen words: 'I have gone astray like a lost sheep; seek Thy servant; for I do not forget Thy commandments.' Astray, and still his.

prayers.title: Bring Me Home Lord Jesus
prayers.why: Paul's own. 'I feel abandoned, far from You. I know I built the distance with my sin.' Owned without being flagellated.

prayers.title: Prayer of the Publican
prayers.why: 'God, be merciful to me a sinner. I stand afar off.' Afar off is where shame puts a man, and the publican prayed from there anyway.

prayers.title: Turn Thy Face From My Sins — Psalm 51
prayers.why: Savonarola, from a prison cell in 1498. Twenty-two words of Psalm 51, and he had a great deal to be ashamed of.

prayers.title: Jesus, Bring Me Back Home
prayers.why: Paul's own, and the return half: bring me back home.

prayers.title: Psalm 51 - Create in Me a Clean Heart
prayers.why: Psalm 51, David's prayer after his worst failure: 'Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation.' Peter went out and wept bitterly, and was restored. Paul's pick, 2026-09-28, in place of an Ephrem prayer that could not be found.

prayers.title: Prayer for Sorrowful Willingness
prayers.why: 'Not yet because I love Thee, but because I fear to lose Thee. Make my imperfect sorrow...' Honest about sorrow that is not yet pure.

prayers.title: Evening Prayer for Pardon
prayers.why: 'Forgive whatever I have this day done amiss.' A nightly return, said again tomorrow -- which is what staying connected after a broken promise actually looks like. (Replaced the Act of Contrition, which is the same prayer as the edition kept at David's Confrontation.)

prayers.title: The General Confession at Holy Communion
prayers.why: For a contrite heart. Contrite, not crushed. SWAPPED 2026-09-02 to the whole confession: the 79-word version this replaced cut off before the mercy, which is the opposite of “contrite, not crushed”.

prayers.title: Way of the Cross - Station 3: Jesus Falls the First Time
prayers.why: Jesus falls the FIRST time. Twenty-nine words about a fall that was not the last word.

prayers.title: O Lord Who Hearest Prayer
prayers.why: 'O Lord, who hearest prayer.' Thirty-three words, for the man who assumes he has used up his hearing.

prayers.title: Cleanse Me, O God, by the Bright Fountain of Thy Mercy
prayers.why: 'Cleanse me by the bright fountain of Thy mercy.' Washing rather than punishment.

prayers.title: Almighty God Have Mercy Upon Us, and Forgive Us All Our Sins
prayers.why: Thirty-one words: have mercy, forgive us all. Nothing itemised, because sometimes he cannot itemise it yet.

prayers.title: An Examination of Conscience
prayers.why: An examination of conscience. Step Ten is this station's primary resonance, and the second fire is where it gets done.

prayers.title: Evening Prayer for Light
prayers.why: An evening prayer for light -- to see what happened before he decides what it means.

prayers.title: Evening Prayers - Examination
prayers.why: Forty-two words of evening examination. Short enough to actually do nightly.

prayers.title: Compline collect: Forgive our trespasses
prayers.why: 'Forgive our trespasses.' The compline collect, said by people who have to get up and try again tomorrow.

prayers.title: O God, Who Dost Bring Men Out of Darkness and the Shadow of Death
prayers.why: 'Who dost bring men out of darkness and the shadow of death.' Out of, which is a direction.

prayers.title: Prayer of St. Bernard for Restoration
prayers.why: Bernard on restoration. Restoration is the word this station needs and 'forgiveness' alone does not cover.

prayers.title: O Lord, Who Dost Wash Out Our Offences
prayers.why: 'Who dost wash out our offences.' Washed out, not held over him.

prayers.title: Though Our Sins Be Seven
prayers.why: 'Though our sins be seven.' Christina Rossetti's line -- though they be seventy times seven.

prayers.title: Verses of Prayer: I have gone astray like a sheep
prayers.why: 'I have gone astray like a sheep.' The same verse in the East Syriac office, sung by a whole church every week.

prayers.title: Prayer of the Penitent Thief — Luke 23:42
prayers.why: The thief's own words from the cross: 'Jesus, remember me.' A robber, and the last word on him was mercy. Paul's pick, 2026-09-28, in place of an invented 'Moses the Black' prayer.

prayers.title: Psalm 50 - Miserere - Have mercy on me O God
prayers.why: Paul's pin. The Miserere -- the psalm David wrote after Nathan said 'you are the man.' The whole thing, from the 1896 Baltimore Manual.

prayers.title: Confiteor - I Confess
prayers.why: The Confiteor: 'through my fault, through my fault, through my most grievous fault.' Said three times, with no second clause anywhere in it.

prayers.title: The Prayer of Manasseh
prayers.why: The Prayer of Manasseh -- a king who did great evil and prayed from the consequences of it. The closest parallel in scripture to this station.

prayers.title: Prayer of Anselm - I Acknowledge My Sin
prayers.why: Anselm: 'I acknowledge my pride, my anger, my envy.' Named as a list, not as a mood.

prayers.title: When I Don't Know What to Pray
prayers.why: To be kept from despair. This station's hope is that consequences can be faced WITHOUT self-destruction being the price -- and this is the prayer that guards it.

prayers.title: My God, I Have Again Given Way to Temper
prayers.why: 'My God, I have AGAIN given way to temper.' One specific act, admitted, with the word again left in.

prayers.title: Prayer Before Confession, for Light to Know My Failings
prayers.why: For light to know my failings -- seeing clearly before speaking, which is the order this station insists on.

prayers.title: Confession - Private
prayers.why: Private confession. Step Five, and the guardrail says a competent guide before any direct disclosure.

prayers.title: Devotions for Confession - Examination of Conscience
prayers.why: Twenty-two words of examination of conscience. Small enough to be done rather than dreaded.

prayers.title: O Lord My God, I Confess That I Have Sinned Against Thee in Thought and Word and Deed
prayers.why: 'I confess that I have sinned against...' Plain, and from men who had no illusions about themselves.

prayers.title: For Confession of Sins Past
prayers.why: For confession of sins past. Past, which is the part that gets buried.

prayers.title: Out of the Deep Have I Called Unto Thee, O Lord: Lord, Hear My Voice
prayers.why: 'Out of the deep have I called unto Thee.' Psalm 130 -- the depth is the honest starting position.

prayers.title: Psalm 37 - Domine ne in furore - O Lord rebuke me not in Thy fury
prayers.why: 'O Lord, rebuke me not in thy indignation.' A penitential psalm that asks not to be destroyed by the truth.

prayers.title: From Mozarabic Sacramentary - Bring Sins to Remembrance
prayers.why: 'Bring my sins to my remembrance, that I may with a lowly heart confess them.' Asking to remember, which nobody does casually.

prayers.title: Prayer of St Ephrem the Syrian – Let Me See My Own Sins
prayers.why: St. Ephrem: grant me to see my own errors and not judge my brother. Mine, not the other person's.

prayers.title: We Confess Our Sins Unto Thee
prayers.why: Confession from the Didache, around AD 80 -- the oldest form of this in the catalog.

prayers.title: Act of Contrition - Traditional Baltimore
prayers.why: The traditional act of contrition. The words most Catholics already know by heart.

prayers.title: Confession of Injury Done to Others
prayers.why: Confession of injury done to OTHERS. The guardrail centres the harmed, and so does this.

prayers.title: Forgive Me, Most Gracious Lord and Father, if This Day I Have Done or Said Anything
prayers.why: 'Forgive me if this day I have...' A daily accounting, before it becomes a decade's.

prayers.title: Litany of Humility - Fear of Being Humiliated
prayers.why: From the fear of being humiliated, deliver me. The hard question here is whether he wants forgiveness while resisting the consequences.

prayers.title: Prayer of Confession - Gelasian Sacramentary
prayers.why: Confession from the Gelasian Sacramentary -- 'through our own grievous fault', in the church's oldest words.

prayers.title: O Lord, Who Art a God Ready to Pardon
prayers.why: 'A God ready to pardon.' Ready -- already, before he has finished the sentence.

prayers.title: Way of the Cross - Station 1: Jesus is Condemned to Death
prayers.why: Jesus condemned. Forty-one words on accepting a verdict without arguing it.

prayers.title: O God, Who Purifiest the Heart of Man From Sin
prayers.why: 'Who purifiest the heart of man from sin.' The purpose of all the naming.

prayers.title: To Confess Voluntary and Involuntary Offences
prayers.why: For offences voluntary and involuntary -- including the harm he did without meaning to, which is most of it.

prayers.title: That I May Never Again Become My Own
prayers.why: Paul's pin. 'That I may never again become my own.' Burning the plow, in one sentence.

prayers.title: Prayer for Open Hands
prayers.why: 'My God, I give Thee all -- my goods, my time, my heart. I make no reserve.' No reserve is this station's hard question: what old equipment is he keeping as a route back.

prayers.title: Final Offering - All to Thee
prayers.why: The final offering, all to Thee. Offered once and not renegotiated.

prayers.title: For Fidelity in Service
prayers.why: For fidelity in service. Elisha poured water on his master's hands for years before anyone handed him anything.

prayers.title: Collect for Strength in Weakness
prayers.why: Thirty-three words: strength in weakness. Step One, which is where the plow-burning actually starts.

prayers.title: Morning Prayer of the Last Elders of Optina - Complete Surrender
prayers.why: The morning prayer of the Optina elders -- from a whole community of guides, not one. The guardrail warns against surrendering judgment to a personality.

prayers.title: For Willingness to Serve
prayers.why: For willingness to serve. The ordinary act of showing up that feels too small to count.

prayers.title: O Lord Jesus, Grant That We Be Not Shaped to the Pattern of This World
prayers.why: 'Grant that we be not shaped to the pattern of this world.' Forty words against the old route staying open.

prayers.title: Dedication and Surrender
prayers.why: Dedication and surrender together -- because either one alone is what this station calls half a decision.

prayers.title: For Faithful Stewardship
prayers.why: For faithful stewardship. Stewardship is what you do with what is not yours.

prayers.title: Morning Surrender to Providence
prayers.why: Morning surrender to providence. Every morning, which is how the years get done.

prayers.title: That Our Lives May Show Forth Service
prayers.why: That our lives may show forth service -- lives, not announcements.

prayers.title: Prayer for Belief
prayers.why: For belief. Step One's shelf is thin and this is one of its eight; a man at the plow needs it as much as anyone.

prayers.title: Prayer for Willing Obedience
prayers.why: For willing obedience. Willing, which is the difference between a disciple and a follower.

prayers.title: Collect for Walking in Thy Way
prayers.why: For walking in Thy way -- walking, one ordinary step of participation at a time.

prayers.title: Make Us, O Lord, to Flourish Like Pure Lilies
prayers.why: 'Make us to flourish like pure lilies.' Forty words, and a reminder that growth is not something he manufactures.

prayers.title: That We May Practice What We Believe
prayers.why: That we may practise what we believe. The gap this station lives in.

prayers.title: Morning Offering of Self
prayers.why: The morning offering of self. Offered at the start, before the day argues.

prayers.title: To Spend Our Lives in Thy Service
prayers.why: To spend our lives in Thy service. Spend -- the plow was worth something and he burned it anyway.

prayers.title: O Lord, Renew Our Spirits, and Draw Our Hearts Unto Thyself
prayers.why: 'Renew our spirits, and draw our hearts unto Thee.' Drawn, rather than driven.

prayers.title: That We May Please Thee
prayers.why: Thirty words: that we may please Thee. Another of step one's eight.

prayers.title: Stir Up, We Beseech Thee, O Lord, Our Hearts
prayers.why: 'Stir up our hearts.' Forty words for the morning the small act feels pointless.

prayers.title: Prayer to Know and Do Thy Will
prayers.why: To know and to do Thy will. Both halves, in that order.

prayers.title: The Morning Collect for Peace, shortened, with a step-twelve close - Book of Common Prayer
prayers.why: For willing obedience and service -- to principles held in common, which is what the guardrail asks for.

prayers.title: Most Merciful Redeemer, Friend and Brother
prayers.why: 'Most merciful Redeemer, Friend and Brother.' Twenty-six words. When the guide leaves, fails or dies, this One does not.

prayers.title: For Trust in God's Providence
prayers.why: Paul's pin. For trust in God's providence. NOTE: this is one of the two acceptance litanies on his rework list -- when he edits the text, this station picks the change up automatically, because the list points at the id.

prayers.title: Prayer Toward the Unknown
prayers.why: Paul's own, from the original twenty-one: a prayer toward the unknown. Abraham went out not knowing where he went, and this is that in a paragraph.

prayers.title: The Path Ahead Is Dark
prayers.why: 'The path ahead is dark.' Says it out loud instead of promising him a map.

prayers.title: Prayer for Guidance in Doubt
prayers.why: For guidance in doubt. Doubt named as the condition, not as a failure to be repented of.

prayers.title: May God Give Us Light to Guide Us, Courage to Support Us, and Love to Unite Us
prayers.why: Twenty-two words: light to guide us, courage to support us. Enough for a day with no visible road.

prayers.title: Kidan Ze-Nege: Covenant Prayer of the Morning
prayers.why: Paul's own -- the Ethiopian Covenant Prayer of the Morning. This station's one next action is a portable daily practice, and here is one that has travelled for centuries.

prayers.title: For Trustfulness
prayers.why: For trustfulness. Trusting is a practice here, not a feeling that arrives.

prayers.title: O Lord, Whose Way Is Perfect
prayers.why: 'O Lord, whose way is perfect.' Forty-eight words for the man tempted to improve on it with a shortcut.

prayers.title: Brother Lawrence - Presence Prayer
prayers.why: Brother Lawrence, practising the presence of God among the pots and pans. The most portable practice ever written down.

prayers.title: Prayer for Morning Guidance
prayers.why: For morning guidance -- the tent struck and pitched again, one day at a time.

prayers.title: Prayer for Daily Duty
prayers.why: For daily duty. Duty is what travels when certainty does not.

prayers.title: Guide Us in Thy Way, O Lord
prayers.why: 'Guide us in Thy way.' Thirty-six words. Thy way, not the faster one.

prayers.title: Daily Consecration to Providence
prayers.why: Daily consecration to providence. Daily, because yesterday's does not carry over.

prayers.title: O God, Who Makest All Things Work Together for Good
prayers.why: 'Who makest all things work together for good.' Said as trust, not as an excuse for what he did to get there.

prayers.title: Morning Prayer, On Waking
prayers.why: Annie Josephine Levi's morning prayer on waking, 1900. The first thing, before the day starts arguing.

prayers.title: Our Father, Keep Us in Perfect Peace This Day
prayers.why: Thirty-one words: keep us in perfect peace this day. This day is the whole horizon here.

prayers.title: Prayer for Guidance and Discernment
prayers.why: Paul's own, for guidance and discernment -- discernment being what separates a call from a shortcut.

prayers.title: O God, the Protector of All That Trust in Thee
prayers.why: The protector of all that trust in Thee. Protection while he is between places.

prayers.title: Prayer for Divine Guidance - 1900 Manual
prayers.why: For divine guidance, from a 1900 manual. Plain and unmystical, which suits a man who needs a next step and not a vision.

prayers.title: O Lord, I Pray That Thou Wouldest Give Me Grace
prayers.why: 'Give me grace...' Thirty-six words, when waiting has worn through the longer prayers.

prayers.title: Daily Strength - To Be Led
